sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data

stories.headline: Microsoft says Entra Connect Health flaw leaked admin emails
stories.dek: Attackers pulled tenant metadata through a bug that sat in the service's API for nearly four months before Microsoft deployed a fix.
stories.body:
Microsoft is warning organizations that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service to read administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data, BleepingComputer reports. The flaw sat in the Connect Health API from July 23 until Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19.

Entra Connect Health is a cloud monitoring service that lets admins track the health and performance of their on-premises identity infrastructure from the Entra admin center. According to a notification sent to admins and shared on Reddit, Microsoft found the bug on November 9 and concluded its investigation on November 20. "We determined that unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level metadata associated with your organization had occurred," the notice says, adding that Microsoft found no unauthorized configuration changes.

The exposed data includes email addresses of tenant technical contacts and administrator accounts, tenant IDs, display names, initial domain names, country and regional information, Entra license tiers, directory sync status and last sync timestamps, and Connect Health onboarding status. The API also returned an expired certificate once used to register Connect Health agents with an internal Microsoft service decommissioned in late 2024. Microsoft says no passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, Active Directory topology details or Azure subscription information were exposed.

Microsoft has not said who exploited the flaw, how many tenants were hit or when attacks began. More than a dozen administrators reported receiving the notice in the Reddit thread, and some managed service providers said they got separate notifications for multiple customer tenants, arriving hours apart. A Microsoft spokesperson confirmed the fix to BleepingComputer and said impacted customers were notified through Azure Service Health, but declined to give further details.

No software update or customer remediation is required. Microsoft does recommend that organizations warn security teams about targeted phishing and social engineering aimed at the exposed addresses, enforce phishing-resistant multifactor authentication on privileged accounts, review Connect Health configurations, and check Entra audit and sign-in logs. The company also published a PowerShell script at aka.ms/ConnectHealth/scripts that shows which types of metadata could have been exposed, though it displays current values rather than what attackers actually accessed.
key_points: Entra Connect Health API flaw introduced July 23, found November 9
Admin emails, tenant IDs, license tiers and sync status exposed
No passwords, tokens or valid keys exposed, Microsoft says
Number of affected tenants and attacker identity undisclosed
stories.why_it_matters: If you administer an Entra tenant, your email address may now sit on a phishing target list alongside accurate details about your setup. Expect convincing lures and make sure admin accounts use phishing-resistant MFA.

sources.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: GnuPG Security Advisory for GPGME

stories.headline: GnuPG patches critical GPGME double free triggered by rogue keys
stories.dek: A crafted OpenPGP key with a very long user ID can leak app data, and remote code execution can't be ruled out.
stories.body:
The GnuPG project has released GPGME 2.3.1 to fix a critical double free bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, that a malicious OpenPGP key with a very long user ID can trigger. The project says the flaw can be used to exfiltrate data from applications, for example via signed data, and that remote code execution can't be ruled out. All software using GPGME before 2.3.0 is affected, whether shared, DLL or statically linked. Examples include most mail clients, many XMPP clients, Samba and Gpg4win.

The bug sits in two functions that read status lines and key listings from gpg. A reallocated buffer pointer is saved only at the end, so an early return leaves a stale pointer that is freed twice.

Johan Carlsson found it. Gpg4win 5.1.2 ships the fix, and statically linked apps need rebuilds.
key_points: CVE-2026-129975 affects all GPGME versions before 2.3.0; the fix is GPGME 2.3.1, and 2.3.0 was never public.
GnuPG says the double free can exfiltrate app data and remote code execution can't be ruled out.
Gpg4win 5.1.2 bundles the fix; statically linked apps must be rebuilt, and GPGMEPP and GPGMEQT need no update.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets

stories.headline: Rackspace Spot breach exposed customer Kubernetes secrets
stories.dek: Attackers used leaked credentials to run pods and read secrets in customer clusters for nearly a day on November 17, Rackspace told customers.
stories.body:
Hackers used leaked credentials to break into Rackspace Spot, the company's managed Kubernetes cloud platform, BleepingComputer reports. In a notification to affected customers, Rackspace says an unauthorized party accessed parts of the platform on November 17 between about 00:20 and 22:00 UTC. The intruders could act as legitimate users, create pods, list nodes and volumes, and read any Kubernetes Secret in affected users' clusters, plus their Spot API and refresh tokens.

Rackspace learned of the breach on November 18 from a customer report. It says it revoked tokens and sessions, removed the rogue pods and rotated keys. Customers must reissue API tokens, fetch new kubeconfig files, rotate stored credentials and check logs back to November 17.

The response also took the Spot console offline for days. Rackspace says service was fully restored on November 21. It has not told BleepingComputer how many customers were hit.
key_points: Attackers used leaked credentials to access Rackspace Spot on November 17, 2026, for roughly 22 hours.
They could create pods and read Kubernetes Secrets and Spot API tokens in affected customer clusters.
Rackspace shut down console access during cleanup and says service was fully restored on November 21.

sources.title: Hackers Breached FBI Crime Database

stories.headline: FBI reportedly breached again, this time its national crime database
stories.dek: CNN reports the FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into NCIC, the records system police use during traffic stops and background checks.
stories.body:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), CNN reports, citing two people briefed on the investigation. It would be the second reported breach of FBI systems in two months. The intrusion was reportedly discovered in recent days. It is unclear when it happened, how the attackers got in, or whether any data was stolen. The FBI has not publicly confirmed the incident.

NCIC is the database local, state and federal agencies use to share records on wanted and missing persons, arrest warrants, stolen vehicles and firearms, and protection orders.

Two months ago, the ShinyHunters extortion group claimed it breached FBI systems through an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft flaw tied to FBIJobs.gov. BleepingComputer says there is no indication the two incidents are connected.
key_points: CNN reports the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its NCIC database, citing two people briefed on the probe.
The FBI has not confirmed the incident, and it is unclear whether any records were stolen.
ShinyHunters claimed an FBI breach two months ago via an Oracle PeopleSoft flaw; no link to the new incident is known.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats

stories.headline: Malicious webpage pulled private chats from Meta Muse, researchers say
stories.dek: NebuSec chained browser and Linux kernel flaws to take over a user's cloud machine, reaching stored credentials, and says all issues are now fixed.
stories.body:
A single malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories without any approval prompt, according to security firm NebuSec. The page could also alter that data and send it to an external server, The Hacker News reports. The work was a lab demonstration, not an attack on real users.

The researchers then chained a flaw in Muse's built-in browser to a Linux kernel bug, taking full control of the user's cloud machine. That reached the credential store for connected accounts, saved files and Sentinel, the monitoring layer meant to gate everything the agent sends out. The attack did not escape that one machine.

NebuSec says it reported the flaws and all were fixed before publication. Meta has not publicly confirmed the fixes or commented.
key_points: NebuSec says a malicious page let Meta Muse leak chats and memories without user approval.
A browser flaw chained with a Linux kernel bug gave full control of the user's cloud machine, including stored credentials.
NebuSec says all flaws were fixed before publication; Meta has not publicly commented.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: Trump wants to ban US companies from building overseas data centers as bans slow development

stories.headline: Trump floats ban or 'tremendous tax' on overseas US data centers
stories.dek: The president says China would exploit foreign facilities, but any tax would need a Congress controlled by the opposing party.
stories.body:
President Donald Trump says he wants to stop US companies from building data centers in other countries, or charge them a "tremendous tax" if they do. Axios reports he has not yet discussed the idea with his cabinet or advisors, according to Tom's Hardware. "We're not allowing data centers to go into other countries because China will take all of them," Trump said.

Tom's Hardware links the idea to a loophole that lets Chinese AI labs reach banned Nvidia chips in overseas data centers. The House passed the Remote Access Security Act to close it in January 2026, but the bill has stalled in the Senate.

At home, more than 500 local data center moratoriums now slow US projects. Only Congress can impose taxes. Foreign data sovereignty rules and latency also push companies to build abroad.
key_points: Trump wants to bar US firms from building data centers abroad or hit them with a "tremendous tax."
Data center moratoriums across the US have passed 500, according to Tom's Hardware.
The House-passed Remote Access Security Act, aimed at Chinese access to banned chips, has stalled in the Senate since January 2026.

stories.headline: GTA 6 sells at least 32.5 million copies after launch
stories.dek: PCMag reports a blockbuster start for Rockstar's open-world sequel, with sales already past the 32.5 million mark.
stories.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI has sold at least 32.5 million copies, PCMag reported on November 20, calling it a blockbuster launch.

The figure follows an earlier launch-day revenue figure of $3.79 billion. It also tops a 30 million sales forecast for the game. Taken together, the numbers point to one of the biggest debuts the industry has seen.

The 32.5 million figure is a floor, not a final count. PCMag's report did not break down sales by platform or region.
key_points: PCMag reports GTA 6 has sold at least 32.5 million copies.
The total beats a 30 million sales forecast.
It follows an earlier launch-day revenue figure of $3.79 billion.

opinion.headline: A 30 fps GTA VI is no reason for PC players to buy a console
opinion.dek: Every console targets 30 fps and GamesBeat's sources point to a PC version in early 2027, so the smart move is patience.
opinion.body:
Rockstar says the PS5 Pro is not powerful enough to run Grand Theft Auto VI at 60 frames per second. Hold on to that detail, because it is easy to lose in a week when Rockstar reported $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales and called the game "the biggest entertainment launch in history." The game targets 30 fps on every console. Tom's Hardware reports 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, and 720p with FSR 4 upscaling on Series S. No console on the shelf gets a higher target.

So here is the advice for a PC player with no console in the house: do not buy one for this game. Wait. A GamesBeat report citing five sources says GTA VI will arrive on PC in the first few months of 2027. Rockstar has not confirmed a PC version, and that caveat is real. But the best available reporting puts the wait at months, and the reviews say this is a game worth playing properly instead of quickly.

Those reviews are about as good as reviews get. GameSpot and IGN both give it 10/10. GamesRadar, Giant Bomb and The Guardian give 5/5. The lowest score in PC Gamer's roundup is Slant's 4.5/5. GameSpot says it "sets the bar for open worlds impossibly high." IGN's Luke Reilly needed 120 hours to finish the story and says vast areas of the map remain unvisited. Some will read that as a reason to rush out and buy. I read it the other way. A 120-hour game is a long commitment, and it deserves better than hardware bought in a hurry at a frame rate that even the PS5 Pro cannot raise.

The strongest objection is that the PC version is a report, not a promise. Rockstar has said nothing official, and GTA 5 took a year and a half to reach PC. Those perfect scores also went to the console version, at 30 fps, so the frame rate clearly does not ruin the game. And the crowd has already moved: Take-Two cites 32.5 million copies, which PC Gamer describes as pre-release sales and MISSIL reports as sold in 24 hours. Waiting means sitting out the conversation, with no guaranteed date for joining it.

All of that is fair, and none of it changes the math. The question is not whether the console version is good. The question is whether a PC player should buy a whole machine to play one game. Newzoo's Emmanuel Rosier told PC Gamer that rising hardware costs have dented console sales, and that "without GTA 6 the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026." This game is the industry's best argument for buying a console right now, which is exactly why the purchase deserves a second look. Even in the bad case, a wait as long as GTA 5's year and a half, the game does not get worse. The early buyer is not getting everything either. Online play is absent at launch, and Twitch's CEO said earlier this year that the online component would launch in 2027. What exactly is the hurry?

Plenty of PC players appear to have reached the same conclusion. In a PC Gamer reader poll, 29 percent said they would play at launch rather than wait for PC. PC Gamer also reports that GTA 5's concurrent players on Steam rose after GTA 6 arrived on consoles, which suggests many are passing the time with the old game. The outlet is holding its own review for the expected PC port.

Be clear about what waiting buys. Nothing is known about how a PC version will run, because Rockstar has not announced one. My prediction, and it is only that, is that a PC release will not be tied to a 30 fps target the way the consoles are. If that turns out wrong, the patient player has lost nothing except a few months. The impatient one has paid for a console. And this is a poor season for impulse hardware: Ars Technica reports Valve is warning it may have to raise Steam Machine prices.

If a PS5 or Xbox already sits under the TV, none of this applies: clear space for a download of up to 212GB, per TechRadar, and play. Everyone else should keep the money and watch for one thing, Rockstar saying the word PC. The game goes into The Game Awards on December 10 with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, so it will stay in the spotlight. Until Rockstar speaks, treat early 2027 as a well-sourced report and nothing more. As Rosier put it, the game's longer-term story "will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online."
opinion.pull_quote: The question is whether a PC player should buy a whole machine to play one game.
opinion.topic: Waiting for GTA VI on PC
opinion.thesis: PC players should not buy a console just to play GTA VI now. Rockstar caps every console, PS5 Pro included, at 30 fps, and GamesBeat's sources point to a PC version in early 2027, though Rockstar has not confirmed one. The perfect review scores make it a game worth playing properly, and for a PC player that argues for patience, not a rushed purchase of a 30 fps console version.
